doc.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009

chapter: Hurricane Katrina and New Orleans today
title: Katrina: his best clarinet survived while he was in California
summary: He was in California working when the flood came and had left his best instrument in the apartment, barely above the water. He returned in early October 2005 to salvage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Almost everything. Yeah. Not quite everything. I could have lost that. It wasn’t where it should have been. It wasn’t with me. It was in the apartment.
Oh you weren’t in New Orleans.

I was in California for work. But because of the climate where I was going I didn’t want to take my best instrument with me, which is this one. So it was there. If it had been a foot higher or if it had been in a different room in the apartment I would have lost it.
How long was it before you could go back?
I went back in October. The flooding was August 29 and I stayed in California close to where I was working until it was okay to come back, and coordinated a sort of a salvage

operation in early October I believe. Yeah, I suppose it would have been late October, or early October when I came back. Because by late October I remember being in New York City, so I know it must have been earlier on in October.
